comments.author: lawpoop
comments.story: Luca, the Ancestor of All Living Things
comments.why: Short video series on RNA world theory and supporting experiments
comments.text: I personally am a fan of the RNA world hypothesis: [LINK] RNA can act as both a store of information, and as an enzyme catalyzing reactions. In this theory, certain sequences of RNA would be the original self-replicating molecules. Over time, variations in their replication would give rise to other enzymes for specialized reactions, and DNA as a pure-data store. Jack Szostak has done an excellent series of short videos on the theory, and he and his students have done a surprising amount of experiments to support the theory. [VIDEO]

comments.author: martythemaniak
comments.story: What's a virus, anyway? The bare-bones basics
comments.why: Cited alongside dissipative structures as related reading
comments.text: Look into "dissipative structures", which are indeed closely linked to thermodynamics. In short, energy gradients (ie, on hydrothermal vents) can cause matter to organize itself into structures that more efficiently dissipate this energy. You can see how the creation of this structure would in turn enable the creation of a new kind of structure that lives on top of that. [LINK] [VIDEO]
